boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UConn traditions, from campus rituals and songs to recurring community events.

cards.title: Start with Convocation
cards.subtitle: Entering-class welcome tradition
cards.notes: Mark the beginning of your UConn experience by attending Convocation with your entering class and taking in the shared welcome moment.
cards.short_summary: A formal first gathering for UConn’s incoming class.
cards.evidence_claim: UConn identifies Convocation as a tradition that begins students’ academic journeys by celebrating with their entering class.
cards.access_notes: Program details and attendance arrangements vary by year; consult current orientation communications.

cards.title: Rub Jonathan’s Nose
cards.subtitle: Jonathan statue outside Gampel Pavilion
cards.notes: Before a tough exam or during a campus visit, stop at the bronze Jonathan statue and join the good-luck nose-rubbing ritual.
cards.short_summary: A shiny-nosed campus superstition centered on the bronze Husky.
cards.evidence_claim: UConn documents rubbing the Jonathan statue’s nose as a ritual for good luck and good grades.
cards.source_title: Good Luck and Good Grades | UConn Magazine
cards.access_notes: The statue is outside Gampel Pavilion; use normal care around event crowds and entrances.

cards.title: Share the One-Ton Sundae
cards.subtitle: Winter Weekend ice-cream tradition
cards.notes: Look for the Winter Weekend program and join the crowd for UConn Dairy Bar ice cream served in a bucket-sized portion.
cards.short_summary: A cold-weather campus gathering built around Dairy Bar ice cream.
cards.evidence_claim: UConn calls the One-Ton Sundae one of its longest-standing traditions and a Winter Weekend favorite featuring campus-made Dairy Bar ice cream.
cards.access_notes: Offered as part of Winter Weekend; confirm the current event schedule and any distribution details.

cards.title: Watch Homecoming Lip Sync
cards.subtitle: Jorgensen Center for the Performing Arts
cards.notes: Add the Homecoming Lip Sync showcase to your calendar to watch campus groups stage elaborate dance routines—or participate with an eligible group.
cards.short_summary: A Homecoming performance tradition featuring campus organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: UConn describes Lip Sync as a Homecoming tradition featuring extravagant dance routines by cultural centers, student clubs, and Greek organizations.
cards.access_notes: UConn’s 2026 Homecoming schedule lists Lip Sync at Jorgensen; check the current Homecoming schedule for entry details.

cards.title: Sled Horsebarn Hill
cards.subtitle: Horsebarn Hill winter tradition
cards.notes: When conditions and campus guidance allow, bring appropriate winter gear and use the hill’s snowy slope for a classic UConn sledding outing.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal use of UConn’s landmark hill as a sledding slope.
cards.evidence_claim: UConn identifies Horsebarn Hill as its slope for sledding and notes its winter purpose.
cards.access_notes: Participate only in suitable weather and follow any campus safety or access notices.

cards.title: Get Muddy at OOzeball
cards.subtitle: North Rec Park mud-volleyball tournament
cards.notes: Form an eligible team, review the rules and release, and register early for UConn’s annual mud-volleyball tournament at North Rec Park.
cards.short_summary: A long-running spring tournament played in mud.
cards.evidence_claim: UConn says OOzeball began in 1984 as an annual Student Alumni Association tradition and lists North Rec Park as its Storrs location.
cards.access_notes: 2026 participation requires registration, a team fee, and all players to be at least 18; spectators should follow event guidance.

cards.title: Catch the Homecoming Parade
cards.subtitle: Homecoming route on Hillside Road, Gilbert Road, and Mansfield Way
cards.notes: Pick a public viewing spot along the announced route and arrive before the parade’s posted start to see a central Homecoming tradition.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled Homecoming procession through the Storrs campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UConn’s 2026 Homecoming schedule includes a parade on Hillside Road, Gilbert Road, and Mansfield Way.
cards.access_notes: The published 2026 parade is September 27 at 1 p.m.; confirm future-year routes and timing on the Homecoming site.

cards.title: Spell It with the Fight Song
cards.subtitle: “UConn Husky” at rallies and games
cards.notes: Learn the “UConn Husky” refrain and its spelled-out ending, then join in when the band leads it at a rally or game.
cards.short_summary: The university fight song with the familiar Connecticut spelling chant.
cards.evidence_claim: UConn’s Athletic Bands identifies “UConn Husky” as the UConn fight song and documents it among songs sung at rallies and football games.
cards.access_notes: Listen for the band’s cue at applicable events; event admission policies vary.

cards.title: Move for HuskyTHON
cards.subtitle: Student-led fundraiser for Connecticut Children’s
cards.notes: Follow HuskyTHON’s current registration and fundraising guidance, then support or join the dance-marathon community focused on Connecticut Children’s.
cards.short_summary: A UConn student philanthropy culminating in a dance marathon.
cards.evidence_claim: UConn identifies HuskyTHON as an annual student-led charity dance marathon started in 2000 for Connecticut Children’s Medical Center.
cards.source_title: UConn Students Raise Record Amount Through ‘HuskyTHON’ | UConn Today
cards.access_notes: Participation, fundraising, and event details change by year; use current HuskyTHON communications before registering.

cards.title: Celebrate Jonathan’s Birthday
cards.subtitle: Student Alumni Association mascot celebration
cards.notes: Watch Student Alumni Association announcements for Jonathan’s Birthday, then join the campus celebration of UConn’s live Husky mascot.
cards.short_summary: An SAA-planned annual celebration for UConn’s mascot.
cards.evidence_claim: UConn’s Student Alumni Association lists planning Jonathan’s Birthday celebration among the duties of its Vice President of Tradition.
cards.source_title: E-Board | Student Alumni Association | UConn Alumni
cards.access_notes: Date, location, and participation details are announced by the Student Alumni Association.
